checks.observation: Caption direction (high→low water) is correct, but the on-screen label 'Cytoplasm (high water)' contradicts the 'Water in' arrow: water entering requires the cytoplasm to have LOWER water (higher solute) than outside. Label/arrow are mutually inconsistent.
Water entry → vacuole swelling → membrane pressed against rigid wall → turgor pressure → stiffening, wall limits expansion (no lysis). All elements present and consistent.
Hypertonic outside → water leaves → wall prevents shrinkage → membrane detaches (plasmolysis) → turgor lost → wilting. Depiction (inset membrane with gap to wall, shrunken vacuole) matches.

issues: Scene 1 (0-7s): scientific/label contradiction — 'Cytoplasm (high water)' shown alongside a 'Water in' arrow; for osmotic inflow the cytoplasm must be lower in water (higher solute). Relabel or remove the parenthetical.
